objects.description: Small POD-like struct used to hold a candidate guessed word during suggestions: the guessed word text (word), whether it is allowed/valid (allow), and an optional pointer to the original text (orig). Default constructor initializes pointers to nullptr and allow to false. Memory ownership/lifetime of the char* fields is not defined here and should be managed by the caller.
Type alias for a vector of std::string entries, likely representing a mapping entry list. Behaves exactly like std::vector<std::string>.
Type alias for a vector of FLAG values (FLAG is an unsigned short defined by a macro in this header). Behaves like std::vector<unsigned short>.

Container for up to three pattern strings with two associated FLAG condition values (cond and cond2). Default initializes condition flags to FLAG_NULL. String fields default-construct to empty. Ownership of strings is internal; FLAG is an unsigned short via macro.

Packed two-byte character value used by Hunspell to store a 16-bit code unit. Fields l and h hold low and high bytes. Provides implicit conversion to unsigned short and comparison operators. On x86/x64 little-endian, conversion may use std::bit_cast or memcpy; otherwise constructs the value from h:l. Be mindful of packing and endianness when interfacing with raw memory.

Replacement entry holding a pattern and up to four output strings corresponding to medial, initial, final, and isolated forms (likely for script-specific shaping). Owns its std::string members; default compiler-generated constructors/destructor manage memory.
Opaque handle type for a Hunspell instance. This is a forward-declared struct used as a handle in the C API; its contents are intentionally hidden from users of this header.
Forward declaration of the internal implementation class used by Hunspell (pimpl idiom). No definition is provided in this header; it is an incomplete type used only via pointer for encapsulation.

Public C++ API class for Hunspell providing spell checking, suggestion, stemming, morphological analysis/generation, and runtime dictionary modification. It uses a pimpl (HunspellImpl) for implementation hiding. Constructor loads affix and dictionary files; instances are non-copyable and manage internal resources. Some legacy C-style APIs are marked deprecated.
direct_api_constructors: Hunspell(const char* affpath, const char* dpath, const char* key = NULL)

objects.description: cs_info is referenced as a struct in get_csconv() return type, but its definition is not present in this header. It is an incomplete, externally-defined type representing character set conversion info. Details unknown in this header.

functions.name: HUNSPELL_WARNING
functions.signature: static inline void HUNSPELL_WARNING(FILE*, const char*, ...)
functions.description: Conditional warning/logging shim. In this header as provided (without HUNSPELL_WARNING_ON), HUNSPELL_WARNING is a no-op inline function that accepts a FILE* stream, a printf-style format string, and variadic arguments but performs no output. If HUNSPELL_WARNING_ON is defined at compile time, HUNSPELL_WARNING becomes a macro alias to fprintf, and thus can be used to emit formatted warnings to the given stream. Use it like fprintf when warning output is desired; otherwise it compiles out without side effects.
requirements: When compiled with HUNSPELL_WARNING_ON (macro-alias to fprintf): arguments must satisfy fprintf requirements: the FILE* must be a valid stream, the format string must be non-null and correctly describe the provided variadic arguments.
When compiled without HUNSPELL_WARNING_ON (inline no-op): arguments are ignored; behavior produces no output. Other behavioral constraints are unknown.

functions.name: guessword::guessword
functions.signature: guessword::guessword()
functions.description: Default constructor for guessword. Initializes members word and orig to nullptr and allow to false. Used to create an empty guessword instance that the caller can populate with a candidate word (word), an associated flag (allow), and an original string pointer (orig).
requirements: After construction, word == nullptr and orig == nullptr; callers must set these to valid pointers before dereferencing or use.
Ownership and lifetime management of memory pointed to by word and orig are not specified here and are caller-defined/unknown.

functions.name: patentry::patentry
functions.signature: patentry::patentry()
functions.description: Default constructor for patentry. Initializes cond and cond2 to FLAG_NULL; string members pattern, pattern2, and pattern3 are default-constructed empty strings. Intended to hold one or more pattern strings and associated condition flags.
requirements: After construction, pattern, pattern2, and pattern3 are empty; cond and cond2 are FLAG_NULL. Caller should assign appropriate values before use.
No additional constraints are specified in this header; other behavioral details are unknown.

functions.name: w_char::operator unsigned short
functions.signature: unsigned short w_char::operator unsigned short() const
functions.description: Converts a w_char instance to its 16-bit unsigned integer representation. On x86/x64 it uses a bit-level reinterpretation (C++20 std::bit_cast or memcpy fallback); on other platforms it composes the value from the high and low bytes. Use this to obtain the underlying UTF-16/code unit value carried by w_char.
requirements: The w_char object must be valid and initialized before conversion.
Behavior depends on platform endianness handling in the implementation, but the function itself is safe for all supported targets in this header.

functions.name: operator<
functions.signature: bool operator<(const w_char a, const w_char b)
functions.description: Compares two w_char values by their 16-bit unsigned integer value (after converting each via w_char::operator unsigned short). Returns true if a is numerically less than b. Use for strict weak ordering of w_char values (e.g., sorting).
requirements: Both inputs must be valid and initialized w_char values.

functions.name: operator==
functions.signature: bool operator==(const w_char a, const w_char b)
functions.description: Checks equality of two w_char values by comparing their 16-bit unsigned integer representations. Returns true if both represent the same code unit value.
requirements: Both inputs must be valid and initialized w_char values.

functions.name: operator!=
functions.signature: bool operator!=(const w_char a, const w_char b)
functions.description: Checks inequality of two w_char values. Implemented as the logical negation of operator==.
requirements: Both inputs must be valid and initialized w_char values.

functions.name: Hunspell_create
functions.signature: Hunhandle* Hunspell_create(const char* affpath, const char* dpath);
functions.description: Create and initialize a Hunspell handle using the specified affix (.aff) file and dictionary (.dic) file. Use the returned handle with other Hunspell_* APIs and destroy it with Hunspell_destroy when finished.
requirements: affpath must point to a readable Hunspell .aff file.
dpath must point to a readable Hunspell .dic file.
affpath and dpath must be non-null valid C strings.
The returned Hunhandle* must be released with Hunspell_destroy.
Inputs should use the filesystem encoding expected by the runtime/OS.
Thread-safety and reentrancy are unknown; if used across threads, guard externally.

functions.name: Hunspell_create_key
functions.signature: Hunhandle* Hunspell_create_key(const char* affpath, const char* dpath, const char* key);
functions.description: Create and initialize a Hunspell handle using the specified affix and dictionary files, with an additional key parameter (typically for encrypted dictionaries). Use the returned handle with other Hunspell_* APIs and destroy it with Hunspell_destroy.
requirements: affpath must point to a readable Hunspell .aff file.
dpath must point to a readable Hunspell .dic file.
key must be a valid C string appropriate for the dictionary (exact format is unknown).
affpath, dpath, and key must be non-null.
The returned Hunhandle* must be released with Hunspell_destroy.
Thread-safety and reentrancy are unknown; if used across threads, guard externally.

functions.name: Hunspell_destroy
functions.signature: void Hunspell_destroy(Hunhandle* pHunspell);
functions.description: Destroy and free all resources associated with a Hunspell handle created by Hunspell_create or Hunspell_create_key.
requirements: pHunspell must be a handle previously returned by Hunspell_create or Hunspell_create_key.
Call exactly once per created handle; after destruction, pHunspell must not be used.
If there are outstanding suggestion/result lists allocated via this handle, free them first with Hunspell_free_list to avoid leaks.

functions.name: Hunspell_add_dic
functions.signature: int Hunspell_add_dic(Hunhandle* pHunspell, const char* dpath);
functions.description: Load an additional dictionary (.dic) file into an existing Hunspell handle. Returns 0 if more slots remain, 1 if the additional dictionary slots are now full.
requirements: pHunspell must be a valid handle from Hunspell_create/Hunspell_create_key.
dpath must point to a readable .dic file (only dic files are accepted).
dpath must be a non-null valid C string.
May be called multiple times until slots are full (exact slot count unknown).
Return value must be checked to determine if more dictionaries can be added.

functions.name: Hunspell_spell
functions.signature: int Hunspell_spell(Hunhandle* pHunspell, const char* word);
functions.description: Check whether a word is spelled correctly according to the loaded dictionaries. Returns 0 for a misspelled word, non-zero for a correctly spelled word.
requirements: pHunspell must be a valid handle.
word must be a non-null, NUL-terminated C string.
word should be encoded in the dictionary’s encoding (see Hunspell_get_dic_encoding).
Return value must be checked: 0 = bad word; non-zero = good word.

functions.name: Hunspell_get_dic_encoding
functions.signature: char* Hunspell_get_dic_encoding(Hunhandle* pHunspell);
functions.description: Retrieve the dictionary encoding name for the given Hunspell handle (e.g., ISO-8859-1, UTF-8). Use this to encode inputs/interpret outputs appropriately.
requirements: pHunspell must be a valid handle.
Return pointer ownership is unknown; treat as library-owned string and do not free unless documentation elsewhere states otherwise.

functions.name: Hunspell_suggest
functions.signature: int Hunspell_suggest(Hunhandle* pHunspell, char*** slst, const char* word);
functions.description: Generate spelling suggestions for a (typically misspelled) word. On success, returns the number of suggestions and sets *slst to a newly allocated array of C strings (or NULL if the count is 0). Use Hunspell_free_list to free the returned list.
requirements: pHunspell must be a valid handle.
slst must be a non-null pointer to an uninitialized char** variable; *slst need not be initialized.
word must be a non-null C string, preferably in the dictionary’s encoding.
The caller must free the returned list with Hunspell_free_list(pHunspell, slst, n) using the exact count n returned.
If the function returns 0, *slst will be set to NULL.

functions.name: Hunspell_suffix_suggest
functions.signature: int Hunspell_suffix_suggest(Hunhandle* pHunspell, char*** slst, const char* word);
functions.description: Suggest words derived via suffix rules for the given word. Returns the number of suggestions and sets *slst to a newly allocated array (or NULL if 0). Free the results with Hunspell_free_list.
requirements: pHunspell must be a valid handle.
slst must be a non-null pointer to an uninitialized char** variable; *slst need not be initialized.
word must be a non-null C string, in the dictionary’s encoding.
The caller must free the returned list with Hunspell_free_list using the count returned.
If the function returns 0, *slst will be set to NULL.

functions.name: Hunspell_analyze
functions.signature: int Hunspell_analyze(Hunhandle* pHunspell, char*** slst, const char* word);
functions.description: Perform morphological analysis of the given word. Returns the number of analysis strings and sets *slst to a newly allocated array of C strings describing analyses (or NULL if 0). Free with Hunspell_free_list.
requirements: pHunspell must be a valid handle.
slst must be a non-null pointer to an uninitialized char** variable; *slst need not be initialized.
word must be a non-null C string in the dictionary’s encoding.
The caller must free the returned list with Hunspell_free_list using the count returned.
If the function returns 0, *slst will be set to NULL.

functions.name: Hunspell_stem
functions.signature: int Hunspell_stem(Hunhandle* pHunspell, char*** slst, const char* word);
functions.description: Return stems for the given word. Returns the number of stems and sets *slst to a newly allocated array of stem strings (or NULL if 0). Free with Hunspell_free_list.
requirements: pHunspell must be a valid handle.
slst must be a non-null pointer to an uninitialized char** variable; *slst need not be initialized.
word must be a non-null C string in the dictionary’s encoding.
The caller must free the returned list with Hunspell_free_list using the count returned.
If the function returns 0, *slst will be set to NULL.

functions.name: Hunspell_stem2
functions.signature: int Hunspell_stem2(Hunhandle* pHunspell, char*** slst, char** desc, int n);
functions.description: Extract stems from an existing morphological analysis. Provide an array of analysis description strings (desc) and its length (n); returns the number of stems and sets *slst to a newly allocated array (or NULL if 0). Free with Hunspell_free_list.
requirements: pHunspell must be a valid handle.
slst must be a non-null pointer to an uninitialized char** variable; *slst need not be initialized.
desc must be a non-null pointer to an array of n C string pointers representing analyses (e.g., from Hunspell_analyze).
n must be >= 0 and must match the number of elements in desc.
The caller must free the returned list with Hunspell_free_list using the count returned.
If the function returns 0, *slst will be set to NULL.

functions.name: Hunspell_generate
functions.signature: int Hunspell_generate(Hunhandle* pHunspell, char*** slst, const char* word, const char* word2);
functions.description: Generate word forms by analogy using two example words. Returns the number of generated forms and sets *slst to a newly allocated array (or NULL if 0). Free with Hunspell_free_list.
requirements: pHunspell must be a valid handle.
slst must be a non-null pointer to an uninitialized char** variable; *slst need not be initialized.
word and word2 must be non-null C strings in the dictionary’s encoding.
The caller must free the returned list with Hunspell_free_list using the count returned.
If the function returns 0, *slst will be set to NULL.

functions.name: Hunspell_generate2
functions.signature: int Hunspell_generate2(Hunhandle* pHunspell, char*** slst, const char* word, char** desc, int n);
functions.description: Generate word forms based on one base word and an array of morphological description strings. Returns the number of generated forms and sets *slst to a newly allocated array (or NULL if 0). Free with Hunspell_free_list.
requirements: pHunspell must be a valid handle.
slst must be a non-null pointer to an uninitialized char** variable; *slst need not be initialized.
word must be a non-null C string in the dictionary’s encoding.
desc must be a non-null pointer to an array of n C string pointers (morphological descriptions).
n must be >= 0 and must match the number of elements in desc.
The caller must free the returned list with Hunspell_free_list using the count returned.
If the function returns 0, *slst will be set to NULL.

functions.name: Hunspell_add
functions.signature: int Hunspell_add(Hunhandle* pHunspell, const char* word);
functions.description: Add a word to the run-time (in-memory) dictionary. This affects spell checking for the lifetime of the handle.
requirements: pHunspell must be a valid handle.
word must be a non-null C string in the dictionary’s encoding.
The effect is limited to the runtime; persistence to disk is not implied.
Return value conventions are not documented here; treat non-zero/zero semantics as unknown and check project documentation if needed.

word must be a non-null C string in the dictionary’s encoding.
flags must be a non-null C string; exact contents/format are unknown and dictionary-dependent.
desc must be a non-null C string; exact contents/format are unknown and dictionary-dependent.
Return value semantics are not documented here; verify via project documentation.

functions.name: Hunspell_add_with_affix
functions.signature: int Hunspell_add_with_affix(Hunhandle* pHunspell, const char* word, const char* example);
functions.description: Add a word to the run-time dictionary using the affix flags of an example dictionary word so affixed forms of the new word are recognized.
requirements: pHunspell must be a valid handle.
word must be a non-null C string in the dictionary’s encoding.
example must be a non-null C string corresponding to an existing dictionary word whose affix flags will be copied.

functions.description: Remove a word from the run-time dictionary.
requirements: pHunspell must be a valid handle.

functions.name: Hunspell::Hunspell

functions.description: Constructs a Hunspell object by loading the specified affix (.aff) and dictionary (.dic) files. If a key is required by the dictionary, pass it via the key parameter (format/semantics unknown)

data_types.description: A Hunspell .aff file containing affix rules, encodings, and configuration for a dictionary. It is a text file with key-value directives and rule tables.

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Generator for a minimal yet valid Hunspell .aff file. The fuzzer provides two filenames:
# - affpath: should point to a valid-looking .aff text
# - dpath: points to random data, but handle creation typically requires a coherent pair.
# Our task is only to provide a buffer for FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME/FUZZ_PARAM_STR initial data.
# We will emit a plausible .aff file content that Hunspell can parse, covering a range of
# features: SET/FLAG/TRY/WORDCHARS/COMPOUNDMIN/AF/AM/ICONV/OCONV/REP/KEEPCASE/NEEDAFFIX
# and some affix rules (PFX/SFX), plus MAP. Keep size under 4 KiB.
# The content is deterministic with seed but varies to explore paths.

ENCODINGS = [
    "UTF-8",
    "ISO8859-1",
    "ISO8859-2",
    "KOI8-R",
    "CP1252",
]

FLAG_STYLES = ["UTF-8", "long", "num", "ascii"]  # ascii ~ char
# Hunspell recognizes FLAG long|num|utf-8|compound (varies by version). We'll stick to common ones.

TRY_SETS = [
    "etaoinshrdlucmfwypvbgkqjxz",
    "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz'",
    "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz-",
]

WORDCHARS_SETS = [
    "'",
    "-",
    "'’-",
    "0123456789'",
]

# Some simple ICONV/OCONV pairs to exercise conversion tables
ICONV_PAIRS = [
    ("\u2019", "'"),  # right single quote to ASCII
    ("\u00E9", "e"),  # e-acute to e
]

OCONV_PAIRS = [
    ("ss", "ß"),
    ("ae", "ä"),
]

# Replacement table examples
REP_PAIRS = [
    ("teh", "the"),
    ("recieve", "receive"),
    ("adress", "address"),
]

# MAP groups: characters considered equivalent for suggestions
MAP_GROUPS = [
    "oöôóò",
    "aäâáà",
    "eéèêë",
]


def choose(rng: random.Random, arr: List[str]):
    return rng.choice(arr)


def emit_header(rng: random.Random):
    enc = choose(rng, ENCODINGS)
    # Favor common flag styles; avoid exotic ones for compatibility.
    flag = choose(rng, ["long", "num"]) if enc != "UTF-8" else choose(rng, ["UTF-8", "long", "num"]) 
    tryset = choose(rng, TRY_SETS)
    wordchars = choose(rng, WORDCHARS_SETS)
    lines = []
    lines.append(f"SET {enc}")
    lines.append(f"FLAG {flag}")
    lines.append(f"TRY {tryset}")
    lines.append(f"WORDCHARS {wordchars}")
    # Some common dictionary knobs
    lines.append(f"COMPOUNDMIN {rng.randint(2, 5)}")
    lines.append(f"CHECKCOMPOUNDCASE {rng.randint(0,1)}")
    lines.append(f"KEEPCASE")
    lines.append(f"NEEDAFFIX X")  # Define a needaffix flag used by some entries
    return lines


def emit_conv_tables(rng: random.Random):
    lines = []
    # ICONV
    ic = rng.randint(1, len(ICONV_PAIRS))
    lines.append(f"ICONV {ic}")
    for i in range(ic):
        a, b = ICONV_PAIRS[i]
        lines.append(f"ICONV {a} {b}")
    # OCONV
    oc = rng.randint(1, len(OCONV_PAIRS))
    lines.append(f"OCONV {oc}")
    for i in range(oc):
        a, b = OCONV_PAIRS[i]
        lines.append(f"OCONV {a} {b}")
    return lines


def emit_rep_table(rng: random.Random):
    n = rng.randint(1, len(REP_PAIRS))
    lines = [f"REP {n}"]
    for i in range(n):
        a, b = REP_PAIRS[i]
        lines.append(f"REP {a} {b}")
    return lines


def emit_map_table(rng: random.Random):
    n = rng.randint(1, len(MAP_GROUPS))
    lines = [f"MAP {n}"]
    for i in range(n):
        grp = MAP_GROUPS[i]
        lines.append(f"MAP {grp}")
    return lines


def emit_affix_block(rng: random.Random, kind: str):
    # Emit a minimal PFX/SFX rule set.
    # Format:
    # KIND <flag> Y/N <count>
    # KIND <flag> <cond> <strip> <add> <morph>
    lines = []
    # Choose a flag symbol depending on FLAG style; we will use simple letters/numbers.
    # Use A and B for prefixes, X and Y for suffixes to avoid overlap.
    if kind == 'PFX':
        flag = 'A'
        count = 2
        lines.append(f"PFX {flag} Y {count}")
        # Rule 1: add re- at beginning when word starts with vowel
        lines.append("PFX A 0 re .")
        # Rule 2: strip 'un' then add 'in' for alternative negative form
        lines.append("PFX A un in .")
    else:
        flag = 'B'
        count = 3
        lines.append(f"SFX {flag} Y {count}")
        # plural: add s if ends with consonant
        lines.append("SFX B 0 s [^aeiouy].*")
        # past tense: add ed if ends with non-e
        lines.append("SFX B 0 ed [^e].*")
        # comparative: add er for adjectives
        lines.append("SFX B 0 er .*")
    return lines


def emit_af_am_blocks(rng: random.Random):
    # AF: affix flag groups; AM: morphological data classes
    lines = []
    # Define two AF groups referencing our A/B flags
    lines.append("AF 2")
    lines.append("AF A")
    lines.append("AF B")
    # AM: basic POS tags to exercise morph parser
    lines.append("AM 3")
    lines.append("AM pos:NOUN")
    lines.append("AM pos:VERB")
    lines.append("AM pos:ADJ")
    return lines


def emit_try_extra(rng: random.Random):
    # Extra knobs touching suggestion/generation
    lines = []
    lines.append(f"MAXDIFF {rng.randint(1, 5)}")
    lines.append(f"CHECKNUM {rng.randint(0,1)}")
    return lines


def build_aff(seed: int) -> str:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    parts = []
    parts.extend(emit_header(rng))
    parts.extend(emit_conv_tables(rng))
    parts.extend(emit_rep_table(rng))
    parts.extend(emit_map_table(rng))
    parts.extend(emit_af_am_blocks(rng))
    parts.extend(emit_try_extra(rng))
    parts.extend(emit_affix_block(rng, 'PFX'))
    parts.extend(emit_affix_block(rng, 'SFX'))
    text = "\n".join(parts) + "\n"
    # Ensure size limit
    if len(text.encode('utf-8')) > 4096:
        text = text[:4000]
    return text


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    # Produce a valid .aff file content as bytes, encoded in UTF-8.
    # The fuzzing harness will place this into a temp file for FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME.
    aff_text = build_aff(seed)
    return aff_text.encode('utf-8')

import random
import string
from typing import List, Tuple

# Hunspell .dic basics (generic, dictionary-agnostic):
# - First non-empty line is usually an integer count of entries that follow (affects some implementations).
# - Each following line is a word, optionally followed by flags after a separator (e.g., / or \t with key-value morphs).
# - Words may include Unicode; but plain ASCII is widely accepted.
# - Flags format varies (UTF-8, long, numeric, etc.). We will generate several plausible styles while
#   keeping the file valid text and self-consistent with the count.
# - For encrypted dictionaries, content may be ignored by loader unless accompanied by correct key.
#   We still produce syntactically reasonable plaintext entries.
#
# Goals for fuzzer inputs:
# - Small, valid-looking .dic files of varying sizes.
# - Include variety of word forms: ASCII, mixed case, apostrophes, hyphens, diacritics.
# - Include optional flags using common separators and styles to exercise parsing paths.
# - Keep size under 4096 bytes.

MAX_BYTES = 4096

ASCII_LETTERS = string.ascii_lowercase
ASCII_UPPER = string.ascii_uppercase
ASCII_ALPHA = ASCII_LETTERS + ASCII_UPPER
ALNUM = ASCII_ALPHA + string.digits

# Some common diacritics to simulate UTF-8 words (encoded directly in source as UTF-8)
DIACRITICS = [
    "á", "é", "í", "ó", "ú", "ñ", "ü", "ç", "ő", "ű", "ā", "ē", "ī", "ō", "ū",
    "ß", "ø", "å", "ä", "ö", "œ"
]

# Common flag styles used by various aff formats:
#  - slash + letters: word/AB
#  - slash + mixed: word/abC
#  - tab-separated morph fields: word\tpos:noun\tfoo:bar
#  - numeric flags (sometimes): word/123
#  - long flags comma-separated (when FLAG long): word/flag1,flag2
FLAG_LETTERS = list(string.ascii_letters)
MORPH_KEYS = [
    "pos", "tense", "case", "num", "deriv", "dial", "field", "phon", "alt"
]
MORPH_VALS = [
    "noun", "verb", "adj", "adv", "sg", "pl", "past", "pres", "dat", "gen", "fml", "colloq"
]

def rand_word(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Mix of styles: plain, hyphenated, apostrophe, with diacritics, camel case.
    style = rng.choice(["plain", "hyphen", "apos", "diac", "camel", "caps"])
    base_len = rng.randint(2, 12)
    def base_ascii(n: int) -> str:
        return ''.join(rng.choice(ASCII_LETTERS) for _ in range(n))
    if style == "plain":
        return base_ascii(base_len)
    if style == "hyphen":
        left = base_ascii(rng.randint(2, max(2, base_len-1)))
        right = base_ascii(rng.randint(2, 8))
        return f"{left}-{right}"
    if style == "apos":
        left = base_ascii(rng.randint(2, max(2, base_len-1)))
        right = base_ascii(rng.randint(1, 5))
        return f"{left}'{right}"
    if style == "diac":
        pieces = []
        for _ in range(base_len):
            if rng.random() < 0.25:
                pieces.append(rng.choice(DIACRITICS))
            else:
                pieces.append(rng.choice(ASCII_LETTERS))
        return ''.join(pieces)
    if style == "camel":
        word = base_ascii(base_len)
        idx = rng.randint(1, base_len-1)
        return word[:idx] + word[idx:].capitalize()
    if style == "caps":
        return ''.join(rng.choice(ASCII_UPPER) for _ in range(base_len))
    return base_ascii(base_len)

def rand_flags(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    mode = rng.choice(["slash_letters", "slash_mix", "numeric", "longflags", "morph", "none"])  # include none, occasionally
    if mode == "none":
        return ""
    if mode == "slash_letters":
        k = rng.randint(1, 4)
        flags = ''.join(rng.choice(FLAG_LETTERS[:26]) for _ in range(k))
        return "/" + flags
    if mode == "slash_mix":
        k = rng.randint(2, 6)
        flags = ''.join(rng.choice(FLAG_LETTERS) for _ in range(k))
        return "/" + flags
    if mode == "numeric":
        num = rng.randint(1, 9999)
        return f"/{num}"
    if mode == "longflags":
        parts = ["flag" + str(rng.randint(1, 50)) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 4))]
        return "/" + ",".join(parts)
    if mode == "morph":
        # Produce one or more tab-separated key:val fields
        n = rng.randint(1, 4)
        fields = []
        used_keys = set()
        for _ in range(n):
            key = rng.choice(MORPH_KEYS)
            if key in used_keys:
                continue
            used_keys.add(key)
            val = rng.choice(MORPH_VALS)
            fields.append(f"{key}:{val}")
        return "\t" + "\t".join(fields) if fields else ""
    return ""

def make_dic_lines(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> List[str]:
    lines: List[str] = []
    for _ in range(n):
        w = rand_word(rng)
        f = rand_flags(rng)
        lines.append(w + f)
    return lines

def choose_entry_count(rng: random.Random) -> int:
    # Skew towards small but include some medium sizes
    choices = [1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 10, 16, 20, 32]
    weights = [12, 10, 8, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1]
    return rng.choices(choices, weights=weights, k=1)[0]

def maybe_header_count(rng: random.Random, count: int) -> str:
    # Most .dic begin with the count as the first line; include this often
    if rng.random() < 0.85:
        return str(count)
    # Occasionally omit to exercise tolerant parsers
    return ""

def build_dic(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Generate entries, then ensure size bound
    count = choose_entry_count(rng)
    lines = make_dic_lines(rng, count)

    header = maybe_header_count(rng, count)
    out_lines: List[str] = []
    if header:
        out_lines.append(header)
    out_lines.extend(lines)

    data = ("\n".join(out_lines) + "\n").encode("utf-8")

    # Ensure max size; if too big, reduce entries
    if len(data) > MAX_BYTES:
        # Trim lines conservatively
        # Keep header if present, then truncate entry list
        start_idx = 1 if header else 0
        kept: List[str] = out_lines[:start_idx]
        for line in out_lines[start_idx:]:
            candidate = ("\n".join(kept + [line]) + "\n").encode("utf-8")
            if len(candidate) > MAX_BYTES:
                break
            kept.append(line)
        data = ("\n".join(kept) + "\n").encode("utf-8")
    return data


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Occasionally craft special cases to trigger branches:
    special = rng.random()
    if special < 0.10:
        # Minimal dictionary with explicit count and simple entries
        lines = [
            "3",
            "a",
            "I",
            "co-operate/AB"
        ]
        return ("\n".join(lines) + "\n").encode("utf-8")
    elif special < 0.18:
        # Morphology-heavy entries
        lines = [
            "5",
            "run\tpos:verb\ttense:pres",
            "ran\tpos:verb\ttense:past",
            "runner\tpos:noun\tnum:sg",
            "runners\tpos:noun\tnum:pl",
            "running/ING\tpos:verb"
        ]
        return ("\n".join(lines) + "\n").encode("utf-8")
    elif special < 0.24:
        # Diacritics rich entries
        lines = [
            "4",
            "café",
            "fiancée",
            "straße",
            "jalapeño/AB"
        ]
        return ("\n".join(lines) + "\n").encode("utf-8")
    elif special < 0.30:
        # Long flags style
        lines = [
            "4",
            "color/flag1,flag2",
            "colours/flag3",
            "colorize/flag2,flag4",
            "re-color/flag5"
        ]
        return ("\n".join(lines) + "\n").encode("utf-8")

    return build_dic(rng)

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Generator for Hunspell word strings. We want valid, interesting words across
# typical Hunspell dictionaries. Many builds default to UTF-8; we include
# ASCII words, mixed-case, hyphenated, apostrophized forms, numerics, and
# some common accented UTF-8 sequences that appear in dictionaries.
# The fuzzer stubs consume FUZZ_PARAM_STR multiple times per test case; we
# will serialize several candidate strings separated by newlines so the
# harness can slice them as needed.

ASCII_LETTERS = string.ascii_letters
ASCII_LOWER = string.ascii_lowercase
ASCII_UPPER = string.ascii_uppercase
DIGITS = string.digits
PUNCT_SIMPLE = "-'"  # common within words for Hunspell tokenization
PUNCT_EXTRA = "._/"  # sometimes seen in technical terms

# Some common diacritics as UTF-8 (NFC):
UNICODE_WORDS = [
    "café", "résumé", "naïve", "façade", "über", "coöperate", "piñata",
    "jalapeño", "São", "Łódź", "français", "niño", "smörgåsbord", "élève",
    "ångström", "München", "crème", "fiancée", "déjà", "mañana",
]

# Typical affix-affected forms for English-like dictionaries:
AFFIX_BASES = [
    "run", "walk", "try", "carry", "study", "happy", "city", "box",
    "match", "fix", "go", "do", "play", "work", "taste", "beauty",
]
SUFFIXES = ["s", "es", "ed", "ing", "er", "est", "ly", "ness", "ment"]
PREFIXES = ["un", "re", "pre", "non", "anti", "post"]

# Hyphenated and apostrophe patterns
COMPOUND_PARTS = [
    "state", "of", "the", "art", "mother", "in", "law", "well", "known",
    "part", "time", "long", "term", "first", "class"
]
APOSTROPHE_TAILS = ["s", "re", "ve", "ll", "d", "m"]

# Morph description-like snippets sometimes used with generate2/add_with_flags.
# While exact formats are dictionary dependent, providing plausible tokens is useful.
MORPH_SNIPPETS = [
    "is:plural", "po:noun", "po:verb", "tense:past", "case:gen", "der:adj",
    "num:sg", "num:pl", "pos:3rd", "comp", "sup"
]

MAX_TOTAL = 4096


def _rand_word_ascii(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    # Diverse ASCII words: lower, upper, mixed, digits within, punctuation
    styles = [
        lambda: ''.join(rnd.choice(ASCII_LOWER) for _ in range(rnd.randint(1, 12))),
        lambda: ''.join(rnd.choice(ASCII_UPPER) for _ in range(rnd.randint(1, 12))),
        lambda: ''.join(rnd.choice(ASCII_LETTERS) for _ in range(rnd.randint(1, 16))),
        lambda: ''.join(rnd.choice(ASCII_LOWER + DIGITS) for _ in range(rnd.randint(1, 14))),
        lambda: ''.join(rnd.choice(ASCII_LETTERS + DIGITS) for _ in range(rnd.randint(1, 14))),
    ]
    w = rnd.choice(styles)()
    # Occasionally insert simple punctuation inside to mimic words
    if rnd.random() < 0.3 and len(w) > 2:
        pos = rnd.randint(1, len(w) - 2)
        w = w[:pos] + rnd.choice(PUNCT_SIMPLE) + w[pos:]
    if rnd.random() < 0.15 and len(w) > 3:
        pos = rnd.randint(1, len(w) - 2)
        w = w[:pos] + rnd.choice(PUNCT_EXTRA) + w[pos:]
    return w


def _rand_unicode_word(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    return rnd.choice(UNICODE_WORDS)


def _rand_affixed(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    base = rnd.choice(AFFIX_BASES)
    # Y-change or doubling rules can be exercised by forming typical variants
    # Occasionally apply prefix
    if rnd.random() < 0.5:
        base = rnd.choice(PREFIXES) + base
    # Suffix chain: 1-2 suffixes
    suf_chain: List[str] = []
    for _ in range(rnd.randint(1, 2)):
        suf_chain.append(rnd.choice(SUFFIXES))
    return base + ''.join(suf_chain)


def _rand_compound(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    n = rnd.randint(2, 4)
    parts = [rnd.choice(COMPOUND_PARTS) for _ in range(n)]
    s = '-'.join(parts)
    if rnd.random() < 0.4:
        s += "'" + rnd.choice(APOSTROPHE_TAILS)
    return s


def _rand_numeric_word(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    # Words with numbers; also "version-like"
    patterns = [
        lambda: f"{rnd.randint(0,9999)}",
        lambda: f"v{rnd.randint(0,10)}.{rnd.randint(0,20)}",
        lambda: f"RFC{rnd.randint(100,9000)}",
        lambda: f"ISO{rnd.randint(100,9999)}-{rnd.randint(1,20)}",
    ]
    return rnd.choice(patterns)()


def _rand_apostrophe(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    stem = ''.join(rnd.choice(ASCII_LOWER) for _ in range(rnd.randint(2, 8)))
    return stem + "'" + rnd.choice(APOSTROPHE_TAILS)


def _rand_morph_desc(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    # Join a few morph snippets with commas or spaces to look plausible.
    k = rnd.randint(1, 3)
    sep = ',' if rnd.random() < 0.5 else ' '
    return sep.join(rnd.sample(MORPH_SNIPPETS, k))


def _catalog(rnd: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    # Build a pool of strings to satisfy multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR consumers in a run.
    items: List[str] = []
    # Ensure some non-empty default fallbacks the stubs use
    items.extend(["a", "x", "y", "word", "root", "morph", "alpha", "beta", "gamma", "delta", "newword", "wf", "example", "rm", "free"]) 

    # Add a mix of generated words
    gens = [
        _rand_word_ascii,
        _rand_unicode_word,
        _rand_affixed,
        _rand_compound,
        _rand_numeric_word,
        _rand_apostrophe,
    ]
    for _ in range(rnd.randint(12, 24)):
        items.append(rnd.choice(gens)(rnd))

    # Also include some plausible flags/desc strings for add_with_flags
    items.append(''.join(rnd.choice(string.ascii_uppercase) for _ in range(rnd.randint(1, 4))))
    items.append(_rand_morph_desc(rnd))

    # Deduplicate while preserving order
    seen = set()
    out: List[str] = []
    for s in items:
        if s not in seen:
            seen.add(s)
            out.append(s)
    return out


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)

    # Build a newline-separated corpus of candidate strings.
    strs = _catalog(rnd)

    # To help APIs expecting multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls, provide more entries
    # by lightly expanding the set with case variants and suffix tweaks, but keep valid.
    expanded: List[str] = []
    for s in strs:
        expanded.append(s)
        if s.isalpha():
            if rnd.random() < 0.4:
                expanded.append(s.capitalize())
            if rnd.random() < 0.3:
                expanded.append(s.upper())
        if len(s) <= 10 and s.isalpha() and rnd.random() < 0.3:
            expanded.append(s + 's')
    # Truncate to keep within size budget when joined
    joined = '\n'.join(expanded)
    b = joined.encode('utf-8')
    if len(b) > MAX_TOTAL:
        # Trim to limit. Ensure we do not cut mid-UTF-8 by backing up to a newline boundary if possible.
        cut = MAX_TOTAL
        nl = b.rfind(b'\n', 0, cut)
        if nl != -1 and nl > 0:
            cut = nl
        b = b[:cut]
    return b

import random
import struct
import itertools

# Generator for Hunspell "affix flags string" use-cases in add_with_flags APIs.
# We want valid-looking tuples of (word, flags, desc) concatenated into one buffer
# that fuzzer splits via FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls. Since the harness calls FUZZ_PARAM_STR
# three times (word, flags, desc), common fuzzing frameworks split the initial buffer
# on NULs or newlines. We'll produce a single bytes buffer with three NUL-separated
# UTF-8 strings: word\0flags\0desc. This keeps inputs valid and distinct.
#
# Objectives:
# - word: typical dictionary words, mixed case, diacritics, hyphenation, apostrophes.
# - flags: cover common FLAG modes: ASCII single-letter sets, numeric IDs, UTF-8 long flags.
# - desc: plausible morphological descriptions seen in hunspell dicts (e.g., is:plural, po:verb).
#
# Size limit: under 4096 bytes.

ASCII_WORDS = [
    "test", "testing", "color", "colour", "analyze", "analyse",
    "resume", "cafe", "naive", "cooperate", "reenter", "e-mail",
    "email", "foo", "bar", "baz", "qux", "mother-in-law",
    "O'Connor", "don't", "it's", "they're", "child", "children",
]

UNICODE_WORDS = [
    "café", "naïve", "façade", "élève", "niño", "über", "straße",
    "résumé", "coöperate", "São", "İstanbul", "Łódź", "Αθήνα",
    "Москва", "東京", "مكتبة", "हिन्दी", "ไทย", "한국어",
]

# Flag formats to exercise:
# - Classic single-letter flags (e.g., "A", "AB", "XyZ").
# - Comma-separated numeric flags for NUM flag type (e.g., "12,34,256").
# - Long flags (UTF-8 strings) space-separated.
# - Mixed case and duplicates.
FLAG_LETTER_SETS = [
    "A", "AB", "ABC", "XZ", "a", "ab", "AbC", "AEIOU", "RSTLNE",
]

FLAG_NUMERIC_SETS = [
    "1", "12,34", "5,6,7", "10,200,4095", "1024,2048", "255,256,257",
]

FLAG_LONG_SETS = [
    "PLURAL", "VERB PAST", "GERUND", "NOUN MASC", "FEM", "DIMINUTIVE",
    "COMPARATIVE SUPERLATIVE", "PREFIXABLE SUFFIXABLE",
]

# Morphological description patterns often contain key:value pairs separated by spaces.
DESC_TEMPLATES = [
    "is:plural",
    "po:noun",
    "po:verb tense:past",
    "po:adj degree:comp",
    "is:proper is:forbidden",
    "morph:root=%s",  # will substitute a base form
    "deriv:suffix=ness po:noun",
    "deriv:prefix=re po:verb",
    "lang:en",
]

# Some base roots for descriptions
ROOTS = [
    "test", "color", "analyse", "resume", "cafe", "run", "big",
]

# Helper to assemble flags according to a chosen style

def make_flags(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    style = rng.choice(["letters", "numeric", "long", "letters", "numeric"])  # bias to common
    if style == "letters":
        base = rng.choice(FLAG_LETTER_SETS)
        # Occasionally shuffle and deduplicate
        chars = list(base)
        rng.shuffle(chars)
        # allow repeats sometimes
        if rng.random() < 0.3:
            chars = chars + chars[: rng.randint(0, max(0, len(chars) - 1))]
        return "".join(chars)
    elif style == "numeric":
        base = rng.choice(FLAG_NUMERIC_SETS)
        # maybe append one value in range [1,4095]
        if rng.random() < 0.4:
            extra = str(rng.randint(1, 4095))
            return base + "," + extra
        return base
    else:  # long
        base = rng.choice(FLAG_LONG_SETS)
        # maybe add another token
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            base += " " + rng.choice(FLAG_LONG_SETS).split(" ")[0]
        return base

# Helper to assemble a plausible word

def make_word(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    choice = rng.random()
    if choice < 0.55:
        w = rng.choice(ASCII_WORDS)
    elif choice < 0.9:
        w = rng.choice(UNICODE_WORDS)
    else:
        # Construct hyphenated or apostrophe variant
        left = rng.choice(ASCII_WORDS + UNICODE_WORDS)
        right = rng.choice(ASCII_WORDS + UNICODE_WORDS)
        sep = rng.choice(["-", "'", "’"])
        w = left + sep + right
    # Case variations
    mode = rng.randint(0, 3)
    if mode == 1:
        w = w.capitalize()
    elif mode == 2:
        w = w.upper()
    elif mode == 3:
        # Title-like for hyphenated
        w = "-".join([p.capitalize() for p in w.split("-")])
    return w

# Helper for morphological description

def make_desc(rng: random.Random, base_word: str) -> str:
    tmpl = rng.choice(DESC_TEMPLATES)
    if "%s" in tmpl:
        root = rng.choice(ROOTS + [base_word.lower()])
        desc = tmpl % root
    else:
        desc = tmpl
    # Randomly add another kv pair
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        extra = rng.choice([
            "tense:pres", "tense:past", "num:sg", "num:pl", "case:gen",
            "degree:super", "is:forbidden", "is:keepcase",
        ])
        desc = desc + " " + extra
    return desc

# Assemble into NUL-separated strings; this aligns well with common FUZZ_PARAM_STR conventions.

def assemble_buffer(word: str, flags: str, desc: str) -> bytes:
    # Ensure non-empty strings per stub fallback logic so we keep our intended values.
    if not word:
        word = "wf"
    if not flags:
        flags = "A"
    # The C stub for C API enforces non-empty desc via fallback; C++ stub may use empty.
    # We keep desc possibly empty to exercise that path.
    parts = [word, flags, desc]
    # Join with NUL; terminate with NUL to help frameworks that read sequentially.
    data = "\0".join(parts) + "\0"
    b = data.encode("utf-8")
    # Cap to 4096 bytes; if exceeded, trim desc first
    if len(b) > 4096:
        # shorten desc
        max_desc_bytes = max(0, 4096 - (len((word + "\0" + flags + "\0").encode("utf-8")) + 1))
        desc_bytes = desc.encode("utf-8")[:max_desc_bytes]
        b = (word + "\0" + flags + "\0").encode("utf-8") + desc_bytes + b"\0"
        b = b[:4096]
    return b


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    word = make_word(rng)
    flags = make_flags(rng)
    # Randomly pick empty desc to hit the C++ path where empty string is allowed
    if rng.random() < 0.35:
        desc = ""
    else:
        desc = make_desc(rng, word)
    return assemble_buffer(word, flags, desc)

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator crafts valid-looking UTF-8 strings intended for Hunspell word,
# flags, and morphological description parameters, packed into a single bytes
# buffer. Fuzzer stubs will read FUZZ_PARAM_STR (and possibly an unsigned int)
# from this buffer when exercising:
#  - Hunspell_add_with_flags (C API)
#  - Hunspell::add_with_flags (C++ API)
# The stubs expect up to three strings (word, flags, desc), and in the C++ stub
# an unsigned int selector precedes desc. We will encode a simple length-prefixed
# sequence that typical fuzz harnesses accept: [count][entries...], where each
# entry is [u16 length][data]. We also include an optional 4-byte selector after
# the first two strings for the C++ stub.
#
# Strings generated aim to be valid per Hunspell expectations:
#  - word: alphabetic ASCII and some Unicode letters, plus hyphen/apos; lengths vary.
#  - flags: sequences typical for Hunspell aff flags: single letters, multi-letters,
#           or long-form like KEY=VALUE lists; includes ASCII uppercase that many
#           dictionaries use.
#  - desc: morphological description strings like "is:plural", "pos:noun",
#          "tense:past", possibly with multiple semicolon-separated fields.
#
# Total buffer limited to <= 4096 bytes.

MAX_BUF = 4096

ASCII_LETTERS = string.ascii_letters
WORD_PUNCT = "-'"
UNICODE_LETTERS = [
    "á", "é", "í", "ó", "ú", "ñ", "ç", "å", "ø", "ä", "ö", "ü", "ß",
    "ā", "ē", "ī", "ō", "ū", "ă", "ș", "ț", "œ", "Æ", "æ"
]

MORPH_KEYS = [
    "is", "pos", "tense", "number", "case", "gender", "degree", "mood",
    "person", "voice", "deriv", "class", "dialect"
]
MORPH_VALS = {
    "is": ["plural", "past", "gerund", "comparative", "superlative", "proper"],
    "pos": ["noun", "verb", "adj", "adv", "pron", "det"],
    "tense": ["present", "past", "future"],
    "number": ["sg", "pl"],
    "case": ["nom", "acc", "gen", "dat", "abl", "loc", "ins", "voc"],
    "gender": ["m", "f", "n", "c"],
    "degree": ["pos", "comp", "sup"],
    "mood": ["ind", "subj", "imp"],
    "person": ["1", "2", "3"],
    "voice": ["act", "pass"],
    "deriv": ["agent", "dimin", "augment", "collect"],
    "class": ["weak", "strong", "irreg"],
    "dialect": ["us", "uk", "ca", "au"]
}

# Flag styles typical in Hunspell dictionaries
FLAG_STYLES = [
    "single",      # single uppercase letter
    "multi",       # short string of uppercase letters
    "num",         # numeric flags as decimal, comma separated
    "keyvals",     # KEY=VALUE;KEY=VALUE style
    "utf",         # include some non-ASCII just to exercise paths
]


def _rand_choice(rng: random.Random, seq: List[str]):
    return seq[rng.randrange(len(seq))]


def gen_word(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Generate a plausible word with letters, apostrophes, hyphens and some unicode.
    parts = []
    syllables = rng.randint(1, 4)
    for s in range(syllables):
        base_len = rng.randint(2, 6)
        chunk = []
        for _ in range(base_len):
            if rng.random() < 0.12:
                chunk.append(_rand_choice(rng, UNICODE_LETTERS))
            else:
                # Bias toward lowercase alpha
                ch = rng.choice(string.ascii_lowercase)
                chunk.append(ch)
        parts.append("".join(chunk))
    word = "-".join(parts) if rng.random() < 0.2 else "".join(parts)
    # Occasionally add an apostrophe suffix like English possessive
    if rng.random() < 0.15:
        word += "'s"
    # Capitalize sometimes to simulate proper nouns
    if rng.random() < 0.2 and word:
        word = word[0].upper() + word[1:]
    return word[:128] if len(word) > 128 else word


def gen_flags(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    style = _rand_choice(rng, FLAG_STYLES)
    if style == "single":
        return rng.choice(string.ascii_uppercase)
    if style == "multi":
        n = rng.randint(2, 6)
        return "".join(rng.choice(string.ascii_uppercase) for _ in range(n))
    if style == "num":
        n = rng.randint(1, 5)
        nums = [str(rng.randint(1, 2048)) for _ in range(n)]
        return ",".join(nums)
    if style == "keyvals":
        n = rng.randint(1, 4)
        kvs = []
        for _ in range(n):
            key = "".join(rng.choice(string.ascii_uppercase) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3)))
            val = "".join(rng.choice(string.ascii_uppercase + string.digits) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 4)))
            kvs.append(f"{key}={val}")
        return ";".join(kvs)
    # utf style
    n = rng.randint(1, 4)
    return "".join(rng.choice(string.ascii_uppercase) + _rand_choice(rng, UNICODE_LETTERS) for _ in range(n))


def gen_morph_desc(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Create one or more key:value pairs separated by semicolons.
    n = rng.randint(1, 5)
    fields = []
    for _ in range(n):
        key = _rand_choice(rng, MORPH_KEYS)
        vals = MORPH_VALS.get(key, ["x"])  # fallback safe
        val = _rand_choice(rng, vals)
        fields.append(f"{key}:{val}")
    # Occasionally add an extra attribute with equals or plus forms seen in some dicts
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        fields.append(f"stem={gen_word(rng)}")
    if rng.random() < 0.15:
        fields.append("infl:+irreg")
    desc = ";".join(fields)
    return desc[:256] if len(desc) > 256 else desc


def _u16(n: int) -> bytes:
    return n.to_bytes(2, "little", signed=False)


def _u32(n: int) -> bytes:
    return n.to_bytes(4, "little", signed=False)


def _pack_str(s: str) -> bytes:
    b = s.encode("utf-8", errors="strict")
    # length prefix u16; if exceeds, truncate to fit
    if len(b) > 65535:
        b = b[:65535]
    return _u16(len(b)) + b


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Build candidate fields
    word = gen_word(rng)
    # Ensure non-empty word for C stub fallback path avoidance
    if not word:
        word = "wf"

    flags = gen_flags(rng)
    if not flags:
        flags = "A"

    # For the C++ stub, an unsigned int is read to choose empty or fuzzed desc.
    # We'll include a selector that toggles both possibilities across seeds.
    selector = rng.getrandbits(32)

    # Choose whether to provide empty or populated desc primarily via selector LSB
    if selector & 1:
        desc = ""
    else:
        desc = gen_morph_desc(rng)
        if not desc:
            desc = "d"

    # Compose buffer as: count(=3) + word + flags + selector(u32) + desc
    # Many harnesses read FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int) directly from the raw stream,
    # so we place the 4-byte selector right after the first two strings.
    parts = []
    parts.append(_u16(3))  # number of string entries logically available
    parts.append(_pack_str(word))
    parts.append(_pack_str(flags))
    parts.append(_u32(selector))
    parts.append(_pack_str(desc))

    buf = b"".join(parts)
    if len(buf) > MAX_BUF:
        buf = buf[:MAX_BUF]
    return buf
